excerpt: Lydia is France's popular peer-to-peer payment app, launched in 2013. In 2024 its banking side became Sumeria, a free online bank account that pays interest; lydia-app.com now redirects to sumeria.eu.
content:
Lydia started in 2013 as a mobile app for paying friends and running shared money pots, and it became so common in France that "je te fais un Lydia" entered everyday speech. Maddyness reported in April 2025 that the Lydia app has 8 million users, mostly in France, and that the company had raised a total of €235 million, with its last round valuing it at a little over €1 billion. Cyril Chiche is co-founder and leads the group, Lydia Solutions.

Banking became Sumeria. On 2 April 2024 Lydia split its services into two apps: Lydia for payments between friends and money pots, and Lydia Comptes for banking. On 15 May 2024 Lydia Comptes was renamed Sumeria, and its two million users moved to the new app, Journal du Net reported. Sumeria is an online bank account that pays interest on the current account, which Chiche described as a first for a French player, along with a card and an assisted savings programme called Sumeria+. The Lydia app continues separately for paying friends. lydia-app.com, the address on this listing, now redirects to sumeria.eu.

Sumeria's About page says the group has 7 million users, 250 employees and offices in Paris, Lyon, Nantes and Bordeaux, with Cyril Chiche as president. Its homepage says the basic Sumeria account is free provided you make at least one eligible transaction every two months, that the card is free and has no foreign transaction fees, that current accounts earn 2% a year for the first three months and then 1%, and that deposits are protected by France's Deposit Guarantee Fund up to €100,000. Paid plans add more features. Maddyness reported that Chiche was considering all options over five years, including a stock market listing.

Rates and conditions change, so check the official site before opening an account. This profile draws on Sumeria's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the service, and nothing here is paid placement.
